programs.title: Agents Work, Members Govern: A Hands-On Introduction to Agent-Managed DAOs
programs.grade_or_level: Adult continuing education / union chapter training
outcomes: Explain the 'Agents operate; people govern' principle and identify the six human-reserved governance actions
Draft and debate a proposal in a simulated Proposal Forum, reserving final votes for human members
Summarize how agents monitor evidence and route tasks without replacing member decision-making

sessions.activity: Tour the charter: members read the mission and reserved-for-humans list, then map which decisions in their own union must stay member-controlled.
Observe Evidence Monitor and Research Synthesis Agent outputs on a topic chosen by the chapter; discuss what evidence summaries add to bargaining discussions.
Small groups draft a mock proposal with the Proposal & Grant Drafter, debate it, and hold a human-only final vote.
Trace a task through Task Router and Collaborator Scout; members role-play a working group coordinating between decision cycles.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized post-session survey responses and mock proposal voting patterns (no names, IDs, or employer data) contributed to shared models of adult civic-learning outcomes.
programs.consent: Union facilitators obtain written informed consent before the program; participation is voluntary, data is anonymized before sharing, and any member may withdraw their data at any time without workplace consequence.

programs.title: Who Decides? Kids Governing a Robot-Run Village
outcomes: Distinguish tasks agents can do from decisions only people should make
Describe how a DAO charter works using Gonstead.X's five zones
Track a measurable outcome and report progress like the Progress Tracker

sessions.activity: Students read a kid-friendly version of the charter and sort sample decisions into 'agent jobs' vs. 'people-only votes' using the six reserved actions.
Teams draft a classroom proposal (e.g., a school garden) with agent-style drafting help, then debate and vote as the human decision-makers.
Students role-play Task Router and Collaborator Scout to organize a mini-project, practicing coordination between decision cycles.
Students set one measurable outcome for their project, build a simple tracking chart, and present progress to the class.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized, aggregated sorting-game results and proposal drafts (no names, ages, or school identifiers) to help improve shared civics-learning models.
programs.consent: Signed guardian/parent consent forms are required before participation, plus student assent; no individual data is collected, all contributions are anonymized at the classroom level, and guardians may opt out at any time.

programs.title: Evidence-First Governance: Running a Decision Cycle with Agent Support
outcomes: Design a full decision cycle from evidence monitoring to human final vote
Use research synthesis outputs to brief boards without overstating findings
Identify which governance actions must remain human-reserved in their own organization

sessions.activity: Staff work with Evidence Monitor and Research Synthesis Agent outputs on a real NGO topic; practice summarizing evidence honestly, noting gaps and uncertainties.
Draft a funding or program proposal with the Proposal & Grant Drafter; peers critique for accuracy and the drafter never enacts anything.
Map the NGO's own decisions against the six human-reserved actions; draft a mini-charter with measurable outcomes.
Set up progress tracking against one measurable outcome; review the Progress Tracker's format and adapt it for staff reporting.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized decision-cycle designs and aggregated self-assessment scores (organization names and staff identities removed) contributed to shared models of governance-training effectiveness.
programs.consent: Participating organizations sign a data-sharing agreement; staff give individual informed consent, contributions are de-identified before leaving the organization, and any partner may pause or end data sharing.

programs.title: Mission to Measurable Outcomes: A Nonprofit Workshop in the Gonstead.X Zones
programs.grade_or_level: Board members, volunteers, and nonprofit staff (introductory)
outcomes: Translate a mission statement into two or three measurable outcomes
Understand how agents support—but never replace—board authority in a DAO structure
Facilitate a community debate and human-only vote in the Proposal Forum

sessions.activity: Participants study the Gonstead.X charter and mission, then workshop their own nonprofit's mission into measurable outcomes on a charter canvas.
Using the Evidence Monitor's summaries as a model, teams practice turning evidence into one-page briefs for boards and donors.
Each team drafts a proposal with the Proposal & Grant Drafter, debates amendments, and holds a final vote reserved strictly for human participants.
Volunteers simulate a working group coordinated by Task Router between decision cycles; debrief on coordination challenges.
Teams present their measurable outcomes and a simple progress dashboard, mirroring the Progress Tracker's reporting style.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized charter canvases, outcome statements, and aggregated workshop feedback (all organization and participant identifiers removed) to inform shared models of nonprofit governance training.
programs.consent: Facilitators obtain informed consent at registration; data is anonymized before inclusion in shared models, participants may skip any sharing activity, and withdrawal of previously shared anonymized contributions is honored on request where feasible.
